references.text: This sentence serves as a literary framework that ties together the various episodes in Judges and underscores the general state of spiritual decline during this period.
The verse functions as the concrete introduction to the worst episode in Judges, illustrating practically what it means to 'do what is right in one's own eyes'.
This episode shows how the absence of kingship led tribes to take their own initiatives that contradicted God's law, confirming the conclusion in 21:25.
The prophecy in Hosea creates a theological arc by showing that the condition during the period of Judges (without a king) is a warning that will repeat itself as judgment before final restoration.
